## Observed behavior

A one-shot Codex `exec_command` call can reap a background descendant when the call returns, even when the command uses `nohup`, redirects all streams, and runs with stdin from `/dev/null`. In a current-HEAD probe on 2026-08-24:

- the call launched `nohup sh -c 'sleep 1; printf ready > result' … &` and returned a PID;
- after the call returned, the PID was gone;
- after two seconds, the result file was absent and the redirected log was still zero bytes.

This is a native `exec_command` process-lifetime boundary, not a Papercusp work-item or server-side command implementation. `nohup` only changes SIGHUP handling; it does not make a child durable outside the client-managed execution scope.

## Safe execution pattern

Do not use a one-shot `exec_command` call as a detached-job launcher when the child must outlive that call. Run the command in a yielded persistent exec session and retain its `session_id`; poll or write to that same session until it exits. For long or uncertain work, use the documented two-call file-capture pattern only when the process remains inside the persistent session, or use a Papercusp durable background-job surface when the task needs server-side lifecycle management.

A missing output file, empty log, or dead PID after a successful one-shot launch is evidence of this carrier limitation; it is not evidence that the producer command completed successfully.
